content_metadata.description: A detailed demonstration of the human brain dissection process in a medical school anatomy lab.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the fold of dura mater that separates the two cerebral hemispheres?
Which cranial nerve is responsible for the sense of smell?
What is the name of the blood vessel that is cut alongside the optic nerve?
What does the instructor pull back to expose the tentorium cerebelli?
What part of the brain is responsible for balance and coordination?

activities.description: Removing the scalp from the skull
Removing the vault of the skull
Making a sagittal cut in the dura mater and exposing the falx cerebri
Pulling back the falx cerebri and examining the cerebral hemispheres
Lifting the frontal lobes and identifying the olfactory and optic nerves
Cutting the optic nerve and internal carotid artery
Pulling back the temporal lobes and identifying the tentorium cerebelli
Cutting the tentorium cerebelli to expose the cerebellum
Cutting the spinal cord and removing the brain
Examining the brain and identifying its parts

characterInteraction.description: The instructor provides guidance, while the assistants follow instructions and help with the dissection.
The students observe and presumably ask questions (not audible in the video).

scenes.contextualRelevance: The setting is a medical school anatomy lab, focusing on learning and discovery.

narrativeProgression.description: The vault of the skull is removed, revealing the brain encased in the dura mater.
The falx cerebri is exposed, showcasing its role in separating the cerebral hemispheres.
The optic nerve is identified and cut, emphasizing its connection to vision.
The brain is fully removed, providing a complete visual of the organ.
